summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, urostomy, type II diabetes, and polysubstance abuse was admitted after self-inflicting multiple stab wounds to her urostomy site with a screwdriver, reporting she felt 'very very sad.' She underwent an exploratory laparotomy and repair of a small intestinal laceration, along with lysis of adhesions. A Foley catheter was temporarily placed into the urostomy to aid healing. Postoperatively, she developed expected ileus, managed supportively. A loopogram confirmed no leak from the ileal conduit. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, regained bowel function, and was medically stable. Psychiatry and social work addressed her mood disorder, substance use, and housing instability. She was discharged to a wheelchair-accessible shelter with follow-up plans for mental health, primary care, and urology.
